speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: At the first global stocktake at the 28th Conference of the Parties (COP28) last year, the international community collectively moved from setting broad-based net zero targets to taking definitive steps towards implementing decarbonisation solutions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We supported the COP28 Presidency to achieve key outcomes such as accelerating the energy transition in this critical decade, including calling on Parties to recognise that energy efficiency improvement is a critical pathway to decarbonisation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: One of the key initiatives was the Global Renewables and Energy Efficiency Pledge, which called on countries to collectively triple renewable energy capacity and double the global annual average rate of energy efficiency improvements by 2030.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This puts us on track to meeting our solar deployment target of at least two GWp by 2030.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We are also investing in research and development activities in emerging low-carbon fuel technologies, such as hydrogen.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Even as Singapore deploys more solar power, imports low-carbon electricity and develops alternative energy sources, natural gas will continue to play an important role in our energy mix.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The recent launch of the second liquified natural gas (LNG) terminal at Jurong Port will help Singapore meet the growing demand, diversify our sources and enhance our local infrastructure to support the importation of natural gas.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Besides these efforts, energy efficiency is also key to our drive towards sustainability while safeguarding our energy security and ensuring cost competitiveness.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: As a small and open economy, Singapore imports almost all of our energy supply.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This makes it doubly important that Singapore raises our energy efficiency and makes every watt of energy count.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Singapore's energy intensity is comparable to the 11th lowest among 38 Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OCED) countries, according to the latest data from the International Energy Agency.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: With higher energy efficiency, our companies do not have to compromise on their economic productivity even if they do not increase their energy demand.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We must press on to do more with less and to seize every opportunity to improve our energy efficiency.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Today, Singapore drives energy efficiency through a combination of policy instruments and incentives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: First, the cost of electricity is not subsidised.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Pricing energy correctly incentivises businesses and consumers to use electricity efficiently and avoid wasteful consumption.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Second, the carbon tax makes businesses internalise the cost of carbon emissions in their consumption and investment decisions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The pricing of carbon spurs companies to reduce their emissions and energy consumption in a way that makes the most economic sense to them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Carbon tax revenue is then used to support efforts to transition to a decarbonised green economy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Third, incentive schemes, such as the Resource Efficiency Grant for Emissions (REG(E)) and Energy Efficiency Grant (EEG) are available to help big and small companies undertake energy efficiency improvement projects and implement energy-efficient equipment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: These help companies reap energy savings and improve their bottom line.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Fourth, we put in place regulatory frameworks that promote energy efficiency in various sectors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: For example, in the building sector, the Building Control Act was recently enhanced to introduce the new Mandatory Energy Improvement regime, where owners of energy-intensive buildings will be required to conduct an energy audit and implement energy efficiency improvement measures to reduce their energy consumption.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: To help our households become more energy-efficient and reap energy cost savings, we implemented mandatory energy labels and minimum energy performance standards.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Since introducing the labels and standards, the average energy efficiency of energy-intensive household equipment, such as air-conditioners and refrigerators, has improved by 59% and 42% respectively.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The Energy Conservation Act or ECA, is our regulatory tool to enhance industrial energy efficiency.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The ECA was enacted in 2012 to introduce mandatory energy management practices for energy-intensive industrial facilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: These are facilities with energy usage threshold exceeding 54 terajoules in two out of the three preceding calendar years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The ECA was then enhanced in 2017 to strengthen energy management practices and introduce minimum energy efficiency standards (MEES) for industry systems.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Today, the ECA covers every stage of an industrial facility's life, including design and initiation, operations and maintenance, as well as any subsequent expansion plans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Companies are required to review their energy performance from the onset, meet specific energy efficiency requirements for systems and equipment, report their energy performances and continually explore opportunities to enhance energy efficiency.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The EC Bill will require all existing industrial facilities to comply with stipulated MEES for energy-consuming industry systems.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: In enhancing the ECA in 2017, section 26B was introduced to stipulate MEES for energy-consuming industry systems.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: These MEES sought to target energy efficiency improvements at the systems level, as opposed to the equipment level.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This encourages companies to take a holistic approach in optimising and improving the energy efficiency across their system as a whole, which will result in greater energy savings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: To ensure that the standards prescribed are commercially sensible for businesses, the National Environment Agency (NEA) also considers the payback period of these energy-efficient technologies and provides industries with ample lead time before the MEES requirements kick in.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The detailed MEES requirements for chilled water system were developed after close consultation with the industry in 2018.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: NEA announced the MEES for chilled water systems in December 2019.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Based on data reported by companies under the ECA, chilled water systems, which are commonly used by industrial facilities for process or space cooling, account for approximately 16% of electricity consumed in industrial facilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This makes chilled water systems the highest electricity-consuming common system in the industry.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Based on 2016 energy use reported by companies regulated under the ECA, over 70% of these systems were found to be operating at sub-optimal energy efficiency levels.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The MEES for chilled water systems was then set as the energy efficiency benchmark for industry and provides guidance for industrial facilities on how to optimise their systems to achieve higher energy efficiency and cost savings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We implemented the first phase of MEES for chilled water systems by requiring new industrial facilities operational on or after 1 December 2020 to conform to MEES.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Incorporating energy-efficient chilled water systems from the outset reduces the environmental impact of operating a less efficient system throughout its lifespan.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: In addition, this allows facility owners to reap substantial cost savings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: One example is Soitec Microelectronics Singapore, a wafer and semiconductor manufacturing company that has installed an energy-efficient chilled water system in their new building in 2022.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This has helped Soitec Microelectronics save about S$320,000 per year from lower energy use and reduced its carbon emissions by 400 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalence annually.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: All remaining industrial facilities, which are less energy-intensive and not currently regulated under the ECA, will have a longer runway to conform by 1 December 2029 under Phase 3.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: By then, the chilled water systems installed in existing industrial facilities prior to the announcement in 2019 would be at least 10 years old.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: It would make economic sense to switch to more energy-efficient types since it will reach the system's end of life in a few years' time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: It would be timely for the facility owners to carry out retrofit works to enhance their chilled water system to comply with MEES.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: I am heartened that many of the existing facilities have seized the opportunity to meet MEES ahead of the compliance timeline of the second phase.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Stats Chippac Pte Ltd, a semiconductor manufacturing company, is one such example.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Stats Chippac saw the benefits that could be gained from the MEES requirements and has tapped on the REG(E) to upgrade its chilled water system.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The upgrade has improved the energy performance of the chilled water system by 25%, resulting in cost savings of around S$1.5 million per year from lower energy use.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The payback period for its investment was just five years, after factoring in the grant received, which is well within the 15-year lifespan of chilled water systems.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This meant that Stats Chippac stands to save over $15 million in total by upgrading to a MEES-compliant chilled water system.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: To help the industry offset the capital cost of retrofitting their chilled water system, companies can tap on existing Government schemes, such as the REG(E) and the EEG, before the mandatory requirements kick in.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Large manufacturing companies can apply for Economic Development Board's REG(E) to adopt energy-efficient equipment or technologies, including retrofitting their chilled water system.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) can tap on the EEG funds to offset the cost of complying with MEES for their chilled water system.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: They will receive a higher tier of support of up to 70%, capped at $350,000 under the EEG Advanced Tier.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The proposed amendments will also allow us to extend the MEES framework to existing ECA facilities for other energy-consuming systems which are currently under review.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We look forward to continuing the partnership with the industry to jointly unlock more opportunities to improve energy efficiency and reap energy and cost savings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The Bill will also introduce two other housekeeping amendments to the existing ECA requirements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This is to ensure that such development works are held to the same requirements as the other new industrial facilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Requiring Plan Lodgment cases to undergo EEOA at the planning stage helps to ensure that they are energy-efficient from the onset.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This allows them to enjoy more energy cost savings in the long run and avoid costly retrofitting works in the future.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Enhancing industrial energy efficiency is a win-win solution for both businesses and Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have three points of clarification to raise.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My first clarification is on the categories of individuals with duties under the ECA.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Under ECA, every company is required to appoint energy managers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The new section 23A will also require a relevant person with operational control over any energy consuming systems to be registered.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Duties and offences are prescribed for these individuals and relevant corporations.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is less clear what duties company directors and officers bear.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is possible that company directors or officers may be liable if a registered corporation commits an offence with the consent or convenience of the director or officer.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But this is not spelled out clearly in ECA.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This leads to ambiguity over the responsibilities of directors and officers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In other areas, such as workplace safety, the duties of directors and chief executives are clearly provided for.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There is even a code of practice on chief executives and board of directors workplace safety and health (WSH) duties.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: On matters of sustainability and energy, the duties of company leaders are less clear.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Parliamentary Secretary elaborate on the duties of company directors and officers when it comes to energy conservation measures under ECA?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second point is on the long-stop date for report submission.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Prior to the first report submission before the long-stop date, what measures will be taken by NEA to encourage the other industrial facilities to meet and surpass the MEES?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My third and final point is on how the EEOA and MEES reports submitted to NEA are used to encourage improvements in energy performance.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is commendable that we are expanding the scope of reporting to more facilities.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, report submission is not the end in itself.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The ultimate purpose of these reports is to spur improvements in energy performance.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: NEA has shared that for MEES reports, NEA will review the annual average operating system performance and other key performance data of the tube water systems annually.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Parliamentary Secretary explain what NEA will do with the findings of its review?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Will these findings be communicated to companies or published on an aggregated industry-wide level so that companies can benchmark their performances?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: More generally, can the Senior Parliamentary Secretary share what follow-up steps are taken by the Ministry upon reviewing the EEOA and MEES reports submitted, to help companies achieve more efficiency in their energy use?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Notwithstanding these clarifications, I stand in support of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I support the intent of this Bill to enhance energy efficiency.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, I have several clarifications regarding its potential impact on our residents and local businesses.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: First, Mr Speaker, Sir, the expanded registration requirements, ongoing monitoring and potential penalties raises concerns about their impact on small businesses.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How will the Government support small businesses with limited resources to meet these new energy efficiency monitoring requirements?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will the Ministry consider implementing simplified reporting mechanisms tailored to their capacity?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Meanwhile, a multinational corporation would barely notice such a penalty.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Additionally, how would the Ministry ensure that the registration process for these new registrable relevant persons is smooth and efficient?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We need to avoid unnecessary administrative burdens on businesses.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Offering grace periods and flexibility, especially for those with a proven history of compliance, would show a commitment to supporting those already making an effort.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, Mr Speaker, Sir, the requirement for existing systems to meet MEES presents a potential challenge.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Could this lead to unintended consequences, such as increased costs being passed down to consumers, especially in sectors like retail and food and beverage?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Are there lessons and resources from past energy efficiency initiatives that can help develop a targeted support strategy for older facilities?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Third, Mr Speaker, Sir, the Bill's emphasis on energy managers and their role in ensuring compliance leads to more responsibility for these individuals.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How will the Ministry ensure that training for energy managers is accessible to smaller firms, not just large enterprises?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What measures are in place to prevent the concentration of expertise within larger corporations, which would marginalise smaller businesses?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If energy management expertise becomes concentrated solely within large corporations, smaller businesses may fall behind in meeting the new requirements.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This could lead to penalties and the loss of their competitive edge.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Moreover, the need to hire or train energy managers may inadvertently increase manpower costs for SMEs that are trying to tightly manage their overheads.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: For larger businesses, will this requirement make Singapore a less cost-effective location?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Coupled with the expenses to comply with MEES requirements, could this drive towards sustainability hinder our economic attractiveness?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I propose a proactive approach to address this resource disparity.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The Government should partner with community groups, local educational institutions and industry associations to develop and deliver accessible training programmes, specifically for smaller firms.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Subsidised training, online resources and targeted mentorship are just a few examples of how we can empower our SMEs to meet these new challenges.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Furthermore, how will the Ministry ensure that the Director-General's powers to assess and monitor energy efficiency are exercised transparently and fairly?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Clear guidelines and accountability are essential for building trust and ensuring compliance.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The Ministry must clearly define the Director-General's powers, establish transparent assessment criteria and provide mechanisms for businesses to appeal decisions.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Fourth, Mr Speaker, Sir, raising awareness is paramount to help residents and businesses understand how these changes will affect them.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: A lack of awareness could lead to confusion and compliance challenges.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Beyond merely disseminating information, we need to educate stakeholders about the reasons behind these changes.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Highlighting the long-term environmental and financial advantages of energy conservation will promote greater support and motivate a true move towards sustainable practices.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What steps will be taken to ensure that all stakeholders, particularly smaller businesses, are well-informed about the new registration and reporting requirements?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How can the Government cultivate a culture of energy conservation that goes beyond mere regulatory compliance, making a true community-led effort?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Ongoing dialogue is essential for identifying challenges, addressing concerns and adapting our approach, as needed.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Regular public forums and feedback sessions with affected residents and businesses are critical to ensuring that these regulations remain relevant and effective.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Moreover, how will we know if these regulations achieve their intended goals?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The Ministry must establish clear metrics for measuring the impact of these changes on energy consumption, cost savings and environmental outcomes.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: These results must be shared transparently with local communities, rather than being buried in Government reports.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Regular public updates that engage local communities are essential for maintaining accountability and public trust.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In closing, Mr Speaker, Sir, I want to reiterate my support for the EC Bill and its goals.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Nevertheless, it is important that we protect our local businesses, especially our SMEs, as we move towards a more sustainable future.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: To help achieve this, I recommend a few key actions.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This way, expertise does not just sit with larger companies and everyone has a chance to succeed.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is also essential to maintain an ongoing conversation with residents and businesses.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Regular public forums will help us identify any issue and make adjustments, as needed.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Let us remember that energy efficiency should feel like a partnership, not a burden.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We want our local businesses to feel empowered in their journey towards sustainability, not overwhelmed by new regulations.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Together, we can create a strong community where everyone benefits from our commitment to a greener future.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Yip Hong Weng asked if small companies have access to capability-building programmes and services that could help them in the energy efficiency improvement efforts.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I am pleased to share that there are several programmes available today that small companies can access.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: One example is the Singapore Certified Energy Manager programme, which is co-administered by NEA and the Institution of Engineers Singapore.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Another example is the Energy Efficiency Technology Centre (EETC), which is a collaboration between NEA and the Singapore Institute of Technology.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Since its introduction in 2020, it has upskilled engineering students and existing practitioners in industrial energy efficiency.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: By providing low-cost energy assessment services, EETC also supports energy efficiency improvements at SMEs.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: To date, over 40 SMEs and close to 500 professionals and students have benefited from EETC's services and programmes.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: For example, EETC has helped Fuisland Offset Printing (S) Pte Ltd, a printing company, to identify opportunities to reduce idle power usage and to address the inefficiencies of their printers.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This saved Fuisland 24,000 kilowatt hour (kWh) annually.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Fuisland is currently implementing other recommendations across the enterprise to enhance their overall energy efficiency.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This brings me to my second point, on how the Government is supporting and engaging companies to enhance their energy efficiency.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about the funding support that is available to smaller companies, which may have limited resources.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As mentioned in my opening speech, the Government has introduced funding support schemes to help big and small companies undertake energy efficiency improvement projects.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The EEG helps companies by co-funding investment in energy-efficient equipment.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The EEG provides two tiers of support – a base tier to support up to $30,000 for pre-approved energy efficient equipment; and an advanced tier to support companies for larger investments that drive greater energy efficiency.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Yip asked if MEES requirements would result in higher costs for small companies.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In fact, companies stand to reap significant cost savings from energy efficiency improvements, especially with the Government's funding support.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: With the EEG, small companies can achieve a shorter payback period on their investments through the reduced capital costs and enjoy considerable cost savings from lower energy use during the lifespan of the equipment.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: To illustrate, an SME that taps on the EEG to retrofit a chilled water system with a cooling load of 1,000 refrigeration tons would be able to reduce the investment's payback period by about 20% to two years.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Louis Ng and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about efforts to engage the industry on the requirements under the ECA.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Indeed, NEA has engaged the industry on energy efficiency improvements through multiple channels.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This includes working with trade associations and chambers to reach out to companies, particularly SMEs, to raise awareness of how they can make energy efficiency improvements and access funding support through schemes, such as the EEG.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: NEA also organises regular industry engagement sessions and puts out circulars to update the industry on the latest developments and upcoming regulatory requirements, ahead of their compliance timelines.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: NEA adopts a targeted approach through one-on-one engagements with companies to help them understand their performance and identify areas for improvements.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: NEA shares the analysis of how the company's energy efficiency journey compares against the industrial average and encourages companies to adopt industry best practices.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Together, these efforts support companies to take concrete steps to raise their energy efficiency and reduce business costs in the long run.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Louis Ng is right that the energy reports submitted by companies can help to spur energy efficiency improvement at various levels.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The process of preparing the reports enables companies to get facility-level insights, such as its energy performance and potential for energy efficiency improvement.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: NEA also provides support by reviewing each company's energy consumption and their energy efficiency improvement plans, ensuring that these plans are forward-looking, span the next one to five years and include at least one planned energy efficiency measure.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As I mentioned earlier, aggregated data from the reports is used to form the industry average on energy efficiency performance, which is then shared with companies to help them benchmark their own energy efficiency performance.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: NEA is also better able to assess the challenges faced by the industry in improving energy efficiency and assess whether current measures are translating into concrete energy efficiency improvement efforts.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: NEA also has an interest in tracking the overall effectiveness of our energy efficiency measures, as Mr Yip alluded to.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Insights from the energy use reports, together with the EEOA and MEES reports, inform the next bound of policymaking on further energy efficiency gains in industrial facilities.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: For instance, as I shared in my opening speech, the reports highlighted that the majority of the chilled water systems in industrial facilities were inefficient, which led to the introduction of MEES for chilled water systems.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Moving forward, we are also gathering input on the feasibility of applying MEES to other common industrial energy-consuming systems.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Next, I will address questions on key responsibilities and processes under the ECA.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about the duties of company directors under the ECA.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: While company directors do not have specific responsibilities under the ECA, the Energy Conservation (Energy Management Practices) Regulations do prescribe specific responsibilities for the Chief Executive of the company.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Under the Regulations, the Chief Executive is the person principally responsible for the management and conduct of the business of the corporation.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The Chief Executive is required to endorse the corporation's annual submissions to NEA, such as the annual energy use report, energy efficiency improvement plans and energy efficiency opportunities assessment report.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In addition, the Chief Executive is required to provide a signed statement assuring the completeness and accuracy of information submitted for the status of registration of his corporation.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked about the timeline for industrial facilities that are not regulated under the ECA to conform to MEES.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As such, there are no plans to stagger the timeline of report submission over the next five years.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng sought clarifications on the energy efficiency reporting requirements for small companies that fall under the revised definition of "new venture" under the ECA.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: NEA is working with BCA to ensure that companies which have new ventures will be able to complete their EEOA obligations without any delay to the construction of these new ventures.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: NEA is engaging the companies at the early planning stages of their new ventures to help them understand the process and requirements of the EEOA.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng also asked about the registration process of new "registrable relevant persons", which represent the companies required to comply with MEES.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Registration is done on the Emissions Data Monitoring and Analysis portal that companies who have facilities regulated under the ECA are already familiar with.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: They would have used it for past registrations and submissions of their energy use reports.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: NEA will support new companies to familiarise them with the various administrative processes, if needed.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The ECA empowers the Director-General to enforce the MEES, including directing companies to carry out necessary measures to ensure that the prescribed system can meet the prescribed standards.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The NEA Director-General exercises these powers fairly and transparently across the facilities regulated under the ECA.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: NEA has also developed Standard Operating Procedures to ensure that the ECA is implemented consistently and fairly across companies.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: There are also flexibility provisions for companies that face genuine constraints in meeting the requirements of the ECA, which Mr Yip Hon Weng spoke about.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I hope that these clarifications help Members better appreciate these prescriptions and regulations under ECA, which were intended to build essential capabilities within companies for better energy management, while having room to exercise discretion where needed.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This is an important lever for Singapore to reduce our industrial greenhouse gas emissions.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Over recent years, we have made significant strides towards a more sustainable future and enhanced our climate targets.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Our ambitious net zero goal by 2050 requires a major energy transition.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Enhancing our industrial energy efficiency today, is a necessary step to prepare Singapore for a sustainable tomorrow.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, I call on all Members of the House to give your support to this Bill.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: With this, Mr Speaker, Sir, I beg to move.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Yip and Mr Ng, any further clarifications?
